page_summary:
The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick, Volume 1: 1938–1971 is the canonical works record for PKD's letter. It preserves a single archive manifestation and gives the work a stable bibliographic home. The preserved item here is The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick, Volume 1: 1938–1971 (1996). The archive copy runs 374 pages.

structure.form: letter collection, chronologically arranged across more than three decades, with editorial introduction

characters.name: James Blaylock
characters.note: A noted fantasy author and personal friend of Dick's, providing the volume's introduction from firsthand acquaintance.

motifs: A writer's entire early-to-mid career development traced through real-time correspondence rather than retrospective biography
The publisher's built-in caution about the unreliability of third-party claims within the letters
reading.significance: As the earliest and longest-spanning volume in the series, this collection provides essential primary-source insight into Dick's personal, professional, and intellectual development from adolescence through the beginning of his most productive novel-writing period, before any of the theological reorientation of his final decade.
reading.closing_note: Spanning over three decades, this volume captures the full arc of Dick's formation as a writer before the biographical rupture of the early 1970s documented in the following volume.

reading_provenance.note: Close reading of the primary text plus attributed evidence from the archive. Candidate: not yet promoted to canonical.

critical_caution: This is a curated letters volume; the publisher's own note explicitly disclaims the letters as reliable reporting about third parties.
